blog_summary: Adrian Colyer presents two papers from NSDI'20 that tackle system reliability through correlation analysis. The first, Rex, is a tool deployed at Microsoft that prevents bugs and misconfigurations by identifying correlated changes developers often miss. By mining commit logs and using association mining (FP-Growth algorithm), Rex generates change rules that warn developers about files frequently changed together but not updated in tandem. Over 14 months, it caught 4,926 potential issues, including severe service disruptions, by flagging correlated changes in pull requests. The second paper, CloudCanary, focuses on detecting and removing harmful correlations that cause correlated failures. It introduces fault graphs—layered DAGs modeling component dependencies—and uses incremental auditing (SnapAudit) with MinCostSAT solvers to identify minimal risk groups (sets of components whose failure would disrupt the service). DepBooster then generates improvement plans to meet reliability goals. CloudCanary's evaluation on a real-world update trace from a major service provider found numerous risk groups, many of which were confirmed to cause or have caused correlated failures, demonstrating its potential to enhance system resilience.
paper_title: Rex: preventing bugs and misconfiguration in large services using correlated change analysis
paper_abstract: Large services experience extremely frequent changes to code and configuration. In many cases, these changes are correlated across files. For example, an engineer introduces a new feature following which they also change a configuration file to enable the feature only on a small number of experimental machines. This example captures only one of numerous types of correlations that emerge organically in large services. Unfortunately, in almost all such cases, no documentation or specification guides engineers on how to make correlated changes and they often miss making them. Such misses can be vastly disruptive to the service. We have designed and deployed Rex, a tool that, using a combination of machine learning and program analysis, learns change-rules that capture such correlations. When an engineer changes only a subset of files in a change-rule, Rex suggests additional changes to the engineer based on the change-rule. Rex has been deployed for 14 months on 360 repositories within Microsoft that hold code and configuration for services such as Office 365 and Azure. Rex has so far positively affected 4926 changes without which, at the very least, codequality would have degraded and, in some cases, the service would have been severely disrupted.
